title: Technical Lead Onboarding Playbook and Inter-team Handover — First 60 Days
author: Anika Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines a repeatable, cross-functional onboarding and handover process for new technical leads (TLs) joining an engineering team at Redwood Inference. It consolidates hiring touchpoints, a pragmatic first-60-day curriculum, inter-team handover checklist, and a lightweight performance & feedback cadence for managers and peer mentors. The intent is to accelerate impact while preserving knowledge continuity across teams.

Audience:
- New technical leads and their hiring managers
- Peer mentors and direct reports
- People Ops partners supporting role activation
- Hiring panels participating in handoffs and transition interviews

Goals:
- Enable TLs to be independently productive on core deliverables by day 60.
- Reduce knowledge debt and single‑person dependencies during role transitions.
- Standardize expectations for feedback and performance checkpoints.
- Ensure consistent security, access, and compliance handover.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: People Ops (onboarding enablement)
- Role owner: Hiring manager (day-to-day execution)
- Cross-team coordination: Source team manager (outgoing) and destination team manager (incoming)
- Escalation path: Hiring manager -> Director of Engineering -> People Ops partner

Prerequisites (before start date):
1. Offer acceptance and role handbook sent to candidate.
2. Access request ticket created (See "Access & Security checklist" below).
3. Mentor assigned and 1:1 schedule provisioned for first 30 days.
4. First sprint/context docs, architecture maps, and current ROADMAP link shared.

60-day curriculum (week-by-week):
- Week 0 (pre-boarding, 7 days before start):
  - Confirm laptop and environment provisioning (image, VPN, KMS access).
  - Send reading pack: team charter, open PRs, incident history, oncall roster, and sprint board.
  - Quick intro video from outgoing TL if possible (5–10 min).

- Week 1 (orientation & context):
  - Day 1: HR check-in, security briefing, team all-hands, and 30-min manager expectations sync.
  - Set developer environment; validate ability to run test-suite and local server.
  - Shadow 1:1s with each direct report (30m) to capture team priorities and blockers.
  - Deliverable: Update personal onboarding checklist in team wiki.

- Week 2 (codebase immersion & stakeholder map):
  - Read key RFCs/ADRs, review top 5 failing CI tests historically, and exercise a small bug fix.
  - Stakeholder meetings: Product PM, SRE lead, Data/ML counterpart, Security contact.
  - Deliverable: Draft 30/60-day goals and share with manager.

- Weeks 3–4 (ownership & early wins):
  - Lead a small planning session and own at least one low-risk PR to production.
  - Participate in oncall shadowing rotation.
  - Run a 1-hour "architecture walkthrough" for the team.
  - Deliverable: One merged PR and a public post-mortem of the change (short doc).

- Weeks 5–8 (scale leadership & process improvements):
  - Propose one process or tooling improvement (e.g., CI flake reduction, pre-merge tests).
  - Facilitate a cross-team sync to resolve integration gaps.
  - Begin mentoring cycle: schedule recurring 1:1s with direct reports and set career checkpoints.
  - Deliverable: Publish a 60-day readout with risks and hire needs.

Inter-team handover checklist (used by outgoing TL and People Ops):
- Role knowledge transfer:
  - List of active projects with owners, status, and next steps.
  - Architectural diagrams and key RFC/ADR links.
  - Oncall runbook and known incident patterns.
  - CI/CD pipelines and deployment playbooks.

- People and relationships:
  - Current feedback summaries for direct reports (last 6 months).
  - Mentoring relationships and ongoing development plans.
  - Key external stakeholders and SLAs with partner teams.

- Operational and administrative:
  - Access inventory: repos, cloud projects, dashboards, KMS keys (redact secrets - share IDs).
  - Scheduled recurring meetings ownership transfer (calendar updates).
  - Outstanding hiring requests and candidate scorecards.

- Handover acceptance criteria (incoming TL signs off):
  - Able to run the main deployment pipeline with peer present.
  - Can summarize incident escalation flow and key oncall contacts.
  - Validated access to monitoring, error logs, and build artifacts.

Access & security checklist (minimum):
- Accounts to provision (core): GitHub org, CI runner access, GCP project viewer/editor, Sentry, Datadog (read), Console access to model-serving cluster (RBAC session).
- Secrets & KMS: Request per-policy access with approval ticket; do not transfer private keys in email.
- Compliance: If team handles regulated data, confirm egress/VPC config and ensure Private deployment onboarding steps are completed.

Hiring & interview involvement for TLs (expectations):
- Panels: TLs should participate in at least two interview loops within first 60 days (scheduling prioritized by manager).
- Calibration: Attend a 60-minute interview calibration session run by People Ops within week 4.
- Scorecard usage: Use the team’s competency rubric (see table below) and attach high-level notes to the candidate record.

Performance and feedback cadence (manager + TL):
- Week 2: informal 1:1 to confirm onboarding logistics and early blockers.
- Week 4: 30-minute checkpoint to review 30-day goals and early wins.
- Week 8 (end of 60-day period): written 60-day readout and manager evaluation.
- Ongoing: transition into standard 1:1 cadence and quarterly performance cycle.

Quick feedback templates (for managers):
- Positive reinforcement: "In the last sprint, your ownership of X reduced incident MTTR by Y%. I’d like to see you continue to..."
- Constructive: "I noticed X. For the next two weeks, please try Y and schedule a sync so we can iterate."

Competency rubric (one-line criteria used in interview/hire feedback):
| Area | Expectation at TL level | Evidence examples |
|------|-------------------------|-------------------|
| System design | Designs reliable, observable services with clear tradeoffs | Architecture docs, ADR authorship |
| Execution | Drives delivery, unblock teams, lands changes to prod | Merged features, reduced backlogs |
| People leadership | Coaches engineers and enables growth | Mentoring notes, promotion nominees |
| Cross-team influence | Negotiates scope with product and infra partners | Meeting notes, cross-team initiatives |

(Interviewers: capture 1–2 lines of evidence against each area; attach code sample/PR references where relevant.)

Manager guide: how to run the 60-day readout meeting
1. 20 min: TL presents accomplishments, blockers, and risks.
2. 10 min: Manager provides calibrated feedback with examples.
3. 10 min: Agree on updated 90-day objectives and any hiring or resourcing needs.
4. Follow-up: Manager uploads 60-day writeup to People Ops with recommended pulse (pass/needs-development/high-support).

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Failure: TL lacks access to critical repos. Mitigation: Escalate to Cloud Access team within 24 hours; use emergency guest tokens to unblock.
- Failure: Knowledge gaps in oncall expectations. Mitigation: Pair with outgoing TL for two full oncall rotations or escalate to SRE for shadowing.
- Failure: Poor alignment with PM on priorities. Mitigation: Host triage meeting with PM + Director to re-scope objectives.

Templates and artifacts (links & snippets):
- 30/60-day goal template (copy into personal wiki):
  - Objective: "{impact statement}"
  - Success metrics: "{1–3 measurable outcomes}"
  - Risks: "{key assumptions and blockers}"
  - Stakeholders: "{names and roles}"

- 60-day readout doc outline (to upload to People Ops):
  - Summary (3–4 bullet impact statement)
  - Outcomes achieved
  - Open risks and mitigation plan
  - Suggested hires/support requests

- Handover artifact checklist (to attach to acceptance ticket):
  - Link to architecture diagram, list of top-5 PRs, open incidents list, and access inventory CSV.

Related training and resources:
- Recommended e-learning: "Effective Technical Leadership" (internal L&D link), SRE oncall fundamentals, and Redwood security basics.
- Must-read RFCs: list of three team/infra RFCs (attach links in team wiki).

Metrics to track (people + operational):
- Time-to-first-merge (target: <= 21 days)
- Number of knowledge transfer artifacts produced (target: >= 3 by day 30)
- Oncall readiness: observed shadowing shifts completed (target: 2 full shifts)
- Manager satisfaction pulse (People Ops survey at day 60)

Appendix A — Example calendar for first 4 weeks (high level):
- Monday: 1:1 with manager, team standup, environment setup.
- Tuesday: Stakeholder intro meetings.
- Wednesday: Codebase walkthrough and first PR.
- Thursday: Oncall shadow and CI exercise.
- Friday: 30-minute "show and tell" and sync with mentor.

Appendix B — Quick checklist for outgoing TLs:
- Export short bios of direct reports and current development plans.
- Flag technical debt items and label high risk areas.
- Provide schedule of recurring vendor/partner meetings and contractual notes.

Change history:
- 2026-04-15: Created by Anika Patel.
- 2026-05-10: Updated access checklist and added rubric table (reviewers: Diego Morales, Leah Brooks).

If you have questions or need role-specific adjustments, contact People Ops onboarding (people-ops@redwood.com) or the author.
